canonical_data: app definitions, processor run entries, vectorized user data, and chat session data in a relational database
current_repo_note: Covers the open LLMStack repository, not the hosted Promptly cloud offering the README also advertises.
strengths: The agent app type runs a bounded tool-calling loop (a configurable maximum of steps, ten by default) over the processors an app declares, and feeds tool errors back to the model as tool results
A no-code builder, an HTTP API, and Slack and Discord triggers expose the same app definition, so a non-programmer can publish an agent to several surfaces
Multi-tenant organizations, a bundled vector store, and a pip-installable single-command start make a self-hosted trial short
weaknesses: The licence is a custom source-available text that bars offering the software as a hosted or managed service and forbids circumventing its licence-key functionality, so it is not open source
The agent app type's model list is an enumeration of OpenAI models and its provider field is read-only, while other providers appear only as chain processors
The last commit and the last release (v0.2.6) are from late 2024, so current model and tool-protocol support is unreviewed and probably behind
The README documents a default admin account with a published password and the agent loop reviewed has no per-tool approval step
why_it_matters: Shows what a no-code agent builder with its own run history and tenancy looks like, and how a source-available licence restricts hosting it as a service.
